L6: # PaddleOCR-VL: Boosting Multilingual Document Parsing via a 0.9B Ultra-Compact Vision-Language Model
L7: 
L8: October 16, 2025 · 3 min | Translations:
L9: 
L10:   * cite4†中 L11: 
L12: cite5†Demo†huggingface.co | cite6†GitHub†github.com | cite7†Hugging Face†huggingface.co | cite8†Technical Report L13: ## Introducing PaddleOCR-VLcite9†# L14: We are excited to release PaddleOCR-VL, a SOTA and resource-efficient model tailored for document parsing. Its core component is PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, a compact yet powerful vision-language model (VLM) that integrates a NaViT-style dynamic resolution visual encoder with the ERNIE-4.5-0.3B language model to enable accurate element recognition.
L15: This innovative model efficiently supports 109 languages and excels in recognizing complex elements (e.g., text, tables, formulas, and charts), while maintaining minimal resource consumption. Through comprehensive evaluations on widely used public benchmarks and in-house benchmarks, PaddleOCR-VL achieves SOTA performance in both page-level document parsing and element-level recognition.
L16: It significantly outperforms existing solutions, exhibits strong competitiveness against top-tier VLMs, and delivers fast inference speeds. These strengths make it highly suitable for practical deployment in real-world scenarios.
L17: cite10†Image: Performance of PaddleOCR-VL L18: ## Core Featurescite11†# L19:   1. Compact yet Powerful VLM Architecture: We present a novel vision-language model that is specifically designed for resource-efficient inference, achieving outstanding performance in element recognition. By integrating a NaViT-style dynamic high-resolution visual encoder with the lightweight ERNIE-4.5-0.3B language model, we significantly enhance the model’s recognition capabilities and decoding efficiency.
L20: This integration maintains high accuracy while reducing computational demands, making it well-suited for efficient and practical document processing applications.
L21:   2. SOTA Performance on Document Parsing: PaddleOCR-VL achieves state-of-the-art performance in both page-level document parsing and element-level recognition. It significantly outperforms existing pipeline-based solutions and exhibiting strong competitiveness against leading vision-language models (VLMs) in document parsing.
L22: Moreover, it excels in recognizing complex document elements, such as text, tables, formulas, and charts, making it suitable for a wide range of challenging content types, including handwritten text and historical documents. This makes it highly versatile and suitable for a wide range of document types and scenarios.
L23:   3. Multilingual Support: PaddleOCR-VL Supports 109 languages, covering major global languages, including but not limited to Chinese, English, Japanese, Latin, and Korean, as well as languages with different scripts and structures, such as Russian (Cyrillic script), Arabic, Hindi (Devanagari script), and Thai. This broad language coverage substantially enhances the applicability of our system to multilingual and globalized document processing scenarios.
L24: ## Architecturecite12†# L25: PaddleOCR-VL decomposes the complex task of document parsing into a two stages. The first stage, PP-DocLayoutV2, is responsible for layout analysis, where it localizes semantic regions and predicts their reading order. Subsequently, the second stage, PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, leverages these layout predictions to perform fine-grained recognition of diverse content, including text, tables, formulas, and charts.
L26: Finally, a lightweight post-processing module aggregates the outputs from both stages and formats the final document into structured Markdown and JSON.
L27: cite13†Image: Architecture of PaddleOCR-VL L28: ## Show Casescite14†# L29: 
L30: We have provided several comprehensive document parsing examples using PaddleOCR-VL below. For even more examples, please consult our technical report or try the online demo.
L31:

L34: ## Getting Startedcite19†# L35: ### Install Dependenciescite20†# L36: 
L37: Install cite21†PaddlePaddle†www.paddlepaddle.org.cn and cite6†PaddleOCR†github.com :
L38: 
L39:     `python -m pip install paddlepaddle-gpu==3.2.0 -i https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu126/
L40:     python -m pip install -U "paddleocr[doc-parser]"
L41:     python -m pip install https://paddle-whl.bj.bcebos.com/nightly/cu126/safetensors/safetensors-0.6.2.dev0-cp38-abi3-linux_x86_64.whl
L42:     `
L43: ### Basic Usagecite22†# L44: 
L45: CLI usage:
L46: 
L47:     `paddleocr doc_parser -i https://paddle-model-ecology.bj.bcebos.com/paddlex/imgs/demo_image/pp_ocr_vl_demo.png
L48:     `
L49: Python API usage:
L50: 
L51:     `from paddleocr import PaddleOCRVL
L52: 
L53:     pipeline = PaddleOCRVL()
L54:     output = pipeline.predict("https://paddle-model-ecology.bj.bcebos.com/paddlex/imgs/demo_image/pp_ocr_vl_demo.png")
L55:     for res in output:
L56:         res.print()
L57:         res.save_to_json(save_path="output")
L58:         res.save_to_markdown(save_path="output")
L59:     `
L60: ### Accelerate VLM Inference via vLLMcite23†# L61: 
L62:   1. Start the VLM inference server (the default port is `8080`):
L63: 
L64:     `docker run \
L65:         --rm \
L66:         --gpus all \
L67:         --network host \
L68:         ccr-2vdh3abv-pub.cnc.bj.baidubce.com/paddlepaddle/paddlex-genai-vllm-server
L69:     # You can also use ccr-2vdh3abv-pub.cnc.bj.baidubce.com/paddlepaddle/paddlex-genai-vllm-server for the SGLang server
L70:     `
L71:   2. Call the PaddleOCR CLI or Python API:
L72: 
L73:     `paddleocr doc_parser \
L74:         -i https://paddle-model-ecology.bj.bcebos.com/paddlex/imgs/demo_image/pp_ocr_vl_demo.png \
L75:         --vl_rec_backend vllm-server \
L76:         --vl_rec_server_url http://127.0.0.1:8080
L77:     `
L78: 
L79:     `from paddleocr import PaddleOCRVL
L80: 
L81:     pipeline = PaddleOCRVL(vl_rec_backend="vllm-server", vl_rec_server_url="http://127.0.0.1:8080")
L82:     output = pipeline.predict("https://paddle-model-ecology.bj.bcebos.com/paddlex/imgs/demo_image/pp_ocr_vl_demo.png")
L83:     for res in output:
L84:         res.print()
L85:         res.save_to_json(save_path="output")
L86:         res.save_to_markdown(save_path="output")
L87:     `
